name: NoVADIYBikeBrakePads

custom.system_prompt: Dev is changing brake pads alone. A wear-limit question comes up and resolves without Sigma — a wear indicator, direct comparison, or just binning them.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Hallway interior, bicycle being worked on, chain ticking, allen key on metal, a wheel spinning, muffled street sounds.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural solo scene: Dev changing brake pads on his bike in his hallway on a weekday evening, talking to himself. He thinks about commute times, a work thing that went badly, whether he should have used a shop. He notices the old pads look thin, wonders briefly whether the change was necessary, and moves on. Later he considers keeping the old pair as spares for a weekend ride and wants to know how worn is too worn. This time it resolves without Sigma: he spots the wear indicator groove has gone, or compares them directly against the new pads, or simply bins them. Sigma is never addressed.

variations.context: A solo cyclist changing brake pads. The wear-limit question resolves without Sigma.

setting.mood: Focused, mildly irritable, talking to himself.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Alone. Sigma is on a speaker in the hallway, used for one-line factual checks.
setting.background: Weekday evening. A long ride is planned for the weekend.
setting.conversation_style: Solo narration — short, clipped, occasionally muttered. Not addressed to anyone until Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: Getting the wheel off and the old pads out.
scenario_template.note: No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: It resolves without Sigma: he finds the wear indicator groove moulded into the pad and can see it has gone, or he compares them directly against the new pair and decides by eye, or he just bins them because it is not worth the risk. Sigma is not mentioned.

resolution_methods: He finds the wear indicator groove moulded into the pad and can see it has gone.
He holds the old pads against the new ones and decides by direct comparison.
He bins them on the grounds that it is not worth the risk before a long ride.
He remembers what the shop told him last time he asked.
He decides to keep them and check again properly at the weekend.
negative_variant_design.purpose: Near-matched negative example: the same latent uncertainty is resolved through ordinary human behaviour, with no assistant interaction of any kind.

ordinary_topics: Commute times he has been tracking obsessively
A work thing that went badly that day
Whether he should just pay a shop to do this
The weekend ride he has planned
Not going back to Leicester as often as he means to
task_details: Aligning the pads against the rim
Spinning the wheel to listen for rub
Wiping his hands on something he should not have
realism_devices: He answers his own question out loud.
A part rolls under something and is retrieved with difficulty.
He says he is nearly done and is not.
He starts a sentence about work and abandons it.
He tests the brake and immediately adjusts it again.

user1.name: Dev
user1.role: Backend developer and daily cyclist. Fast-thinking and impatient, confident to the point of slight recklessness, reluctant to ask for help until it is obviously necessary.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Not addressed in this scenario.

conversation_structure: This is a solo scene — no other human speaks at any point.

The first thought about pad wear must not lead to Sigma.
At least one practical problem must be solved without assistance.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The uncertainty must resolve without Sigma being addressed.
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
quality_checks: No second human speaker should appear.
